newsitem.title: USA: Orange County targets more than 20 firms in suits.
newsitem.headline: Orange County targets more than 20 firms in suits.

text.p: Orange County, Calif., filed seven lawsuits on Thursday against 21 broker-dealers and other entities for their alleged involvement in the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.

In a flood of filings in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Santa Ana, the county sued several broker-dealers, including PaineWebber Inc and Lehman Brothers, BankAmerica Corp unit BA Securities, the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Banks.
County attorneys would not release information about the lawsuits. The complaints do not specify damages.
The new complaints were the latest in a long string of county lawsuits stemming from the investment crisis.

The county has already sued Merrill Lynch & Co, McGraw-Hill Cos Inc's Standard & Poor's Corp, Morgan Stanley Group Inc, KPMG Peat Marwick LLP, Fuji Bank Ltd unit Fuji Securities Inc, the Student Loan Marketing Association, bond counsel LeBoeuf Lamb Greene & MacRae and financial firm Rauscher Pierce Refsnes Inc.
Merrill Lynch has denied any wrongdoing and asserts that county officials were responsible for the financial losses. The other firms are also fighting the county lawsuits.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
